plain_description: Candle lets you deploy machine learning models in production without the bloat of Python frameworks — cutting server costs and startup times. You can run LLMs, image generators, and speech recognition on CPU or GPU with a small Rust binary. It is built for serverless inference, so you get fast scaling and lower infrastructure overhead.
technical_description: Candle is a minimalist machine learning framework written in Rust that exposes a PyTorch-like tensor API. It implements CPU, CUDA, and WASM backends with optional MKL, Accelerate, and cuDNN acceleration for optimized performance. The framework supports model training and inference, loading models from safetensors, GGUF/GGML, ONNX, and PyTorch formats. It includes a transformer model library, flash attention kernels, ONNX runtime evaluation, and quantization using llama.cpp-compatible types. Integration is via Cargo crate dependency. The project ships example implementations covering LLMs (LLaMA, Mistral, Falcon, Phi, Gemma, Qwen), image generation (Stable Diffusion, Wuerstchen), speech recognition (Whisper), text-to-speech (MetaVoice, Parler-TTS), translation (Marian-MT), code generation (StarCoder), and computer vision (YOLO, SAM).
title: Candle

body: A fast inference library for running LLMs locally on modern consumer-class GPUs
plain_description: Run large language models on your own NVIDIA GPU with fast inference speeds. ExLlamaV2 lets you deploy chatbots and AI applications locally using GPTQ and EXL2 quantized models, making LLM inference practical on consumer-class hardware. No cloud dependence required.
technical_description: ExLlamaV2 is a high-performance LLM inference library optimized for NVIDIA GPUs via CUDA. It supports GPTQ and the proprietary EXL2 quantization formats (2-8 bits per weight), enabling models from 1.1B to 70B parameters to run on consumer GPUs with 8-24 GB VRAM. The dynamic generator provides paged attention via Flash Attention 2.5.7+, dynamic batching, smart prompt caching, and K/V cache deduplication. Integration is through a Python API with support for synchronous, batched, and async streamed generation. The library serves as the backend for OpenAI-compatible APIs and web UIs through separate companion projects.
title: ExLlamaV2

body: Run GGUF models easily with a KoboldAI UI. One File. Zero Install.
plain_description: Run powerful AI models locally on your own computer with zero installation. KoboldCpp bundles everything into a single file that works on Windows, Mac, and Linux — just download and run. It handles text generation, image creation, speech recognition, and more, all without needing an internet connection or cloud subscription.
technical_description: KoboldCpp is a self-contained AI inference server built on llama.cpp, supporting GGML and GGUF model formats for LLM text generation. It provides multiple API endpoints including a KoboldAI-compatible API, an OpenAI-compatible API at /v1, and additional endpoints for image generation (Stable Diffusion 1.5, SDXL, SD3, Flux), speech-to-text (Whisper), text-to-speech (Qwen3TTS, Kokoro, OuteTTS), and video generation (WAN 2.2). The single-file executable bundles all dependencies and runs on CPU with optional GPU offloading via CUDA, Vulkan, Metal, or HIPBLAS. It includes a bundled KoboldAI Lite web UI with chat, adventure, instruct, and storywriter modes, MCP server support, tool calling, RAG via TextDB, and Tavern character card loading.
title: koboldcpp

plain_description: Run powerful AI models on your own hardware — no cloud subscription needed. llama.cpp lets you chat with, serve, and experiment with hundreds of open-source LLMs locally on almost any device, from laptops to servers. The big picture: private, offline AI inference that's fast, free, and under your control.
technical_description: llama.cpp is a C/C++ inference engine for large language models (LLMs) that runs on CPU, GPU (NVIDIA CUDA, AMD HIP, Apple Metal, Vulkan, SYCL, Intel OpenVINO, Qualcomm Hexagon, and more). It loads models in the GGUF format and provides a CLI tool (llama-cli), an OpenAI-compatible HTTP server (llama-server), and a WebUI. The server exposes REST endpoints for chat completions, embeddings, reranking, and supports speculative decoding, grammar-constrained generation, and multimodal inputs. Quantization from 1.5-bit to 8-bit reduces memory footprint. Bindings exist for Python, Node.js, Go, Rust, Java, C#, Swift, and others.
title: llama.cpp

body: Distribute and run LLMs with a single file.
plain_description: Run any open-source LLM on your own computer with a single executable file — no setup, no cloud dependency, no installation required. Just download, make it executable, and run. It also includes a built-in speech-to-text tool (whisperfile) for audio transcription and translation from the same single-file package.
technical_description: llamafile packages LLM inference (via llama.cpp), model weights (GGUF format), and an HTTP server into a single cross-platform executable using Cosmopolitan Libc. It runs natively on x86_64 and ARM64 systems across Windows, macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, and OpenBSD with no runtime dependencies. The executable supports CPU and GPU acceleration, includes a built-in server for model serving, and bundles whisperfile for speech-to-text transcription and translation. Quantized models (e.g., Q8_0) are supported out of the box.
title: llamafile

body: LocalAI is the open-source AI engine. Run any model - LLMs, vision, voice, image, video - on any hardware. No GPU required.
plain_description: Run any AI model — LLMs, vision, voice, image, and video — entirely on your own infrastructure, no GPU required. One self-hosted engine with drop-in OpenAI, Anthropic, and ElevenLabs API compatibility. Built-in user management, AI agents, fine-tuning, and distributed scaling — all while keeping your data private.
technical_description: LocalAI is an open-source AI serving engine that loads LLMs, vision, voice, image, and video models behind a single REST/gRPC API. The core is written in Go; each model engine (llama.cpp, vLLM, whisper.cpp, diffusers, MLX, etc.) runs as an isolated gRPC process in C++, Python, or Rust, shipped as a separate OCI image and pulled on demand. It exposes drop-in OpenAI-compatible endpoints for chat, embeddings, audio transcription, TTS, image generation, and vision, plus Anthropic and ElevenLabs API compatibility. GPU acceleration covers NVIDIA CUDA 12/13, AMD ROCm, Intel oneAPI, Apple Silicon Metal, and Vulkan, with CPU-only fallback. The project includes distributed horizontal scaling with VRAM-aware routing via NATS and PostgreSQL, MCP-based autonomous agents with tool use and RAG, fine-tuning via TRL with auto-export to GGUF, on-the-fly quantization, PII redaction, voice recognition, face detection, and a React-based administrative Web UI with i18n.
title: LocalAI

body: Universal LLM Deployment Engine with ML Compilation
plain_description: The big picture: MLC LLM lets you run large language models on nearly any device — laptop, phone, or web browser — without needing a cloud server. Here's why it matters: you get fast, private, on-device AI with OpenAI-compatible APIs. The bottom line: one engine to deploy LLMs everywhere.
technical_description: MLC LLM is a machine learning compiler and high-performance deployment engine for large language models. It uses MLCEngine, a unified inference runtime that compiles models via TVM and TensorIR for GPU backends including CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan, Metal, OpenCL, and WebGPU. The engine exposes an OpenAI-compatible API through REST, Python, JavaScript, iOS, and Android bindings, enabling cross-platform deployment with a single optimized codebase.
title: MLC LLM

body: MLX: An array framework for Apple silicon
plain_description: MLX lets you build and run machine learning models on Apple silicon with minimal code changes. It offers familiar NumPy-like APIs, unified memory across CPU and GPU, and supports training and deploying models efficiently on Mac hardware.
technical_description: MLX is an array framework for machine learning on Apple silicon, developed by Apple machine learning research. It provides Python, C++, C, and Swift APIs with NumPy-like semantics, along with higher-level packages (mlx.nn, mlx.optimizers) that mirror PyTorch. The framework features lazy computation with dynamic graph construction, composable function transformations (automatic differentiation, vectorization, graph optimization), and a unified memory model that allows operations on CPU or GPU without data transfer. MLX supports multi-device execution (CPU and GPU) and includes a CUDA backend for Linux. It is available via pip on macOS and Linux.
title: MLX

body: Get up and running with Kimi-K2.6, GLM-5.2, MiniMax, DeepSeek, gpt-oss, Qwen, Gemma and other models.
plain_description: Run hundreds of open-source AI models on your own hardware with zero cloud dependency. The big picture: download, install, and start chatting with models like Gemma, DeepSeek, Qwen, and Llama in minutes. Here's why it matters: no subscription, no API keys, and full data privacy — everything runs locally on your machine. The bottom line: a single binary that handles model management, inference, and API access so you and your team can experiment with AI without vendor lock-in.
technical_description: Ollama bundles a local LLM server, CLI, and model distribution into a single Go binary. It uses llama.cpp as its core inference backend with GGUF model format, providing CPU and GPU acceleration via NVIDIA CUDA and Apple Silicon Metal. The server exposes a REST API on localhost:11434 for chat, generation, embedding, and model lifecycle management, with official Python and JavaScript client libraries. Deployment options include bare-metal installers for macOS, Windows, and Linux, a Docker image on Docker Hub, and Kubernetes via a Helm chart. The project supports image generation via an experimental sub-system and offers OpenAI-compatible API endpoints through the openai/ package.
title: Ollama

body: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework for large language models and multimodal models.
plain_description: SGLang is a high-performance serving framework that powers trillions of tokens daily for leading AI companies across 400,000+ GPUs. It handles large language models and multimodal models on any hardware—NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Google TPU, or Ascend NPU. The bottom line: production-tested inference at scale, trusted by xAI, NVIDIA, AMD, and more.
technical_description: SGLang is an open-source serving framework for large language models (LLMs) and multimodal models. It provides a Python runtime with RadixAttention for efficient prefix caching, a zero-overhead CPU scheduler, prefill-decode disaggregation, speculative decoding, and structured output generation. The runtime exposes an OpenAI-compatible API and supports tensor, pipeline, expert, and data parallelism across distributed GPU clusters. It integrates with Hugging Face, supports AWQ and GPTQ quantization, and runs on NVIDIA GPUs, AMD GPUs, Intel Xeon CPUs, Google TPUs, and Ascend NPUs.
title: SGLang

body: The official API server for Exllama. OAI compatible, lightweight, and fast.
plain_description: TabbyAPI lets you run powerful open-source LLMs on your own hardware with a simple API that works just like OpenAI's. It's built specifically for ExLlama models, giving you fast inference with features like tool calling, structured output, and concurrent users. The bottom line: get private, low-latency AI without depending on external services.
technical_description: TabbyAPI is a FastAPI-based inference server for ExLlamaV3 models that exposes an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint for text generation and embeddings. It uses a continuous batching engine with paged attention for concurrent request handling on NVIDIA Ampere+ GPUs. The server supports speculative decoding via draft models, JSON schema / Regex / EBNF constrained generation, and OAI-style tool/function calling with Jinja2 template support. Deployment is available via Docker (CUDA image on GHCR) or bare metal, with model loading from HuggingFace or local storage.
title: TabbyAPI

body: TensorRT LLM provides users with an easy-to-use Python API to define Large Language Models (LLMs) and supports state-of-the-art optimizations to perform inference efficiently on NVIDIA GPUs. TensorRT LLM also contains components to create Python and C++ runtimes that orchestrate the inference execution in a performant way.
plain_description: TensorRT-LLM helps you run large language models and visual generation models faster on NVIDIA GPUs, cutting inference costs while boosting throughput. It gives you a simple Python API to define and optimize models, plus ready-made runtimes for production deployment. The bottom line: get more tokens per second with less hardware.
technical_description: TensorRT-LLM is an open-source library that optimizes LLM and visual generation inference on NVIDIA GPUs. It provides custom CUDA kernels for attention, GEMMs, and MoE operations, along with algorithmic runtime optimizations such as Prefill-Decode disaggregation, Wide Expert Parallelism, and Speculative Decoding. The library exposes a high-level Python LLM API built on PyTorch, supporting single-GPU through multi-node deployments with built-in parallelism strategies. It integrates with NVIDIA Dynamo and Triton Inference Server for production serving.
title: TensorRT-LLM

body: Large Language Model Text Generation Inference
plain_description: Deploy and serve the most popular open-source LLMs at production scale without building inference infrastructure from scratch. TGI powers Hugging Face's own products with continuous batching, token streaming, and an OpenAI-compatible API built in. The bottom line: faster AI feature delivery backed by a battle-tested inference engine.
technical_description: Text Generation Inference (TGI) is a Rust, Python, and gRPC server for deploying and serving large language models. It consists of a Rust-based router and a Python inference server running optimized transformers code with custom CUDA kernels. TGI supports Tensor Parallelism across multiple GPUs via NCCL, continuous batching for throughput, token streaming over Server-Sent Events (SSE), and Paged/Flash Attention. Quantization is supported through AWQ, GPTQ, bitsandbytes, EETQ, Marlin, and fp8. The server exposes REST/gRPC endpoints and an OpenAI Chat Completion API-compatible Messages API. It is instrumented with OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing and Prometheus for metrics. Models are loaded via Hugging Face transformers using safetensors.
title: Text Generation Inference

body: A high-throughput and memory-efficient inference and serving engine for LLMs
plain_description: vLLM is the fastest and most cost-effective way to serve large language models at scale. It slashes inference costs through state-of-the-art throughput and smarter memory management with PagedAttention. The bottom line: deploy any LLM in production with lower latency and lower infrastructure bills.
technical_description: vLLM is a high-throughput, memory-efficient inference and serving engine for large language models. It implements PagedAttention for efficient KV-cache management, continuous batching, chunked prefill, and prefix caching. The engine supports distributed inference via tensor, pipeline, data, expert, and context parallelism across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs as well as CPUs, TPUs, and NPUs. It provides an OpenAI-compatible API server, Anthropic Messages API, and gRPC endpoints. vLLM supports 200+ model architectures from HuggingFace, multiple quantization formats (FP8, INT4/8, GPTQ, AWQ, GGUF), speculative decoding (EAGLE, DFlash), structured output generation via xgrammar or guidance, and multi-LoRA serving.
title: vLLM
